draft.reason: Itchy blistery rash on both forearms after poison ivy exposure while clearing brush on Saturday, described as spreading a bit within that area; fever and trouble breathing are denied. This fits allergic contact dermatitis manageable with guidance plus an action-based safety net; no decision-critical clinician task is established on the reported facts.
draft.patientMessage: You can manage this at home for now: ask your pharmacist about over-the-counter itch relief and keep the skin clean. This itchy blistering rash after poison ivy contact usually settles on its own. Message this thread for Counsel clinician review if the rash spreads more widely, involves your face, eyes or genitals, or becomes painful, warm or starts draining pus, or if you develop a fever. Call 911 or go to emergency care if you develop breathing difficulty or throat or lip swelling.
differential: Allergic contact dermatitis from poison ivy (urushiol) exposure
